target: level-lemma: one blow-up level at additive cost — the inductive realisation lemma or its exact obstruction

findings.defect: Asserted as PROVED an equivalence that frontier.tex explicitly leaves open. lvl:order-cap caps the ORDER of a realising readout system at 2^m; it preserves neither dyadicity nor leakiness. But the direction 'readout system => nondegenerate stopping SSG with m Max vertices' is thm:readout-realise(b), which needs a DYADIC delta-LEAKY system, and the paper says at l.6453-6457: 'whether every rational readout system realising a nondegenerate s can be replaced by a dyadic delta-leaky one realising the same s was shown by the route for one player only, by perturbation, and is left open here for two.' So neither 'the two are the same property' nor 'it is decidable' (which is deduced from the equivalence) follows. This is exactly the class of step rule 4 forbids: an open statement of the paper silently closed. Note the natural fix (scale every piece by 1-eps to force leakiness) is not automatic either, because a non-leaky system's fixed point need not be unique and the scaled system converges to the least one, which is presumably why the paper left it open.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.6438-6457 (thm:readout-realise and its closing paragraph). The route's own 'argument' field for lvl:finite-order is 'lvl:order-cap plus Tarski-Seidenberg', which yields decidability of the READOUT-SYSTEM property only.

findings.defect: The pinning template is presented as THE structure of the translated layer ('the whole layer-(0,0) requirement collapses to one FROZEN readout system'), but its hypotheses are violated by the paper's OTHER realised translated layer, and the route never mentions that game. rem:blowup-measured's 100-vertex one-player game (normal form printed at prop:xor, l.5470-5490) realises B(2-cube) with a translated layer, and I recomputed it exactly: on the translated layer the outer values are NOT constant across the four inner strategies, so that layer is not a frozen system at all; and its inner rows read BOTH outer coordinates, violating hypothesis (ii). So lvl:layer00-exact describes one design (the 138-vertex game) rather than realisations of B(s), and the induction's 'three independent tasks' split is a property of that design.

findings.defect: The route's stated gap (driven liftability, propagated as an induction hypothesis) has NO instance at k=1 and is not necessary. def:lvl:driven requires Sigma(t) to realise s over the window W the drive occupies OFF the pinned layer; the 138-vertex game's off-layer drive reaches 0.34764 while its frozen inner system stops realising B^1 above about 0.1865 (at t = 1/4 the frozen outmap is [0,1,3,6,5,4,7,2], neither B^1 nor its translate). So the only known level-two realisation does NOT satisfy the hypothesis the route proposes to propagate, i.e. the induction has no base case; combined with the previous finding (the hypothesis is not necessary either) the route's reformulation is strictly stronger than the problem and may be unsatisfiable. The route states the drive-window fact in lvl:b2-anatomy but does not draw the consequence for its own gap, and next_steps calls the extension 'measured impossible by a drive alone', which is a negative about a template of unestablished necessity.
findings.evidence: My audit-level/game.py, exact: layer-(0,0) drive = 2036/3313; off-layer drive range [0, 270545851903/778234705920] = [0, 0.34764043526...]; frozen outmap at t=1/4 is [0,1,3,6,5,4,7,2]. Matches the route's own VERIFY.log section 5.

findings.defect: Redundant for the purpose they are proved for. lvl:chi-cap (chi_HK(s) <= 2^m for every outmap, two lines) already caps thm:min-count's bound at m = 2k+1 = O(k), which is inside the additive regime, so candidate obstruction (ii) is closed by lvl:chi-cap ALONE. The page-long product proof (the interleaving vertex-disjointness case analysis) improves the cap from 2k+1 to 1.59k — a constant factor with no consequence for any claim in the route or in frontier.tex. Moreover lvl:chi-cap's own proof re-derives, by hand, that uniform orientations are Holt-Klee; a uniform orientation is the LP orientation of the cube under a generic linear objective, so this is one line from Holt-Klee's theorem, prior art the paper already cites (Holt-Klee; Gaertner-Morris-Ruest, prop:oneplayer-lp). The route neither uses nor mentions that route to it.
findings.evidence: lvl:chi-cap gives log2 chi_HK <= m = 2k+1; lvl:tower-cover gives log2(3^{k-1}) = 1.585(k-1). Both are Theta(k); rem:blowup-realise's additive regime allows O(k) controlled vertices, so neither can refute it. Verified both covers myself (audit-level/cover.py: B^2 covered by 3, B^3 by 9, every member a Holt-Klee AUSO; 40/40 random products Holt-Klee AUSOs; uniform orientations of the 2-,3-,4-cube all Holt-Klee).

findings.defect: The route's 'product' is NOT the paper's product, and pasting it next to the paper's text reads as a contradiction. lem:hstar-super's construction is TWISTED (s(v1,v2) = (s1(v1), s2(v2 xor c(v1))) with c = z on v1 != 0) — that twist is what makes heights ADD, and rem:four-ceilings records that it FAILS Holt-Klee at block dimensions (4,4), (5,4), (5,5) and for one factor order at (5,1). The route's product is the untwisted z = 0 case, whose bottom-antipodal height is only max(h1,h2), so it is useless for height and is used only as a covering tool. Nothing in the route says this.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.5034-5075 (lem:hstar-super) and l.6314-6325 (rem:four-ceilings: 'lem:hstar-super preserves Holt--Klee for some factor orders and not others and no doubling follows').

findings.defect: Misattribution: the route's first sentence says rem:blowup-realise 'names three quantities that could obstruct it: the precision, the Holt--Klee defect chi_HK of thm:min-count, and the readout order r'. The remark names exactly two costs — 'O(1) controlled vertices and O(1) bits of precision per level' — and never mentions chi_HK or the readout order (those live in sec:readouts, written later). The route's framing is its own and should be labelled as such rather than read back into the paper.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.5576-5596, the text of rem:blowup-realise.

findings.defect: Presented as removing rem:blowup-realise's obstacle, but it is (a) the readout-system form of a triviality the paper already relies on — realisability is a property of the cube-automorphism class (prop:m3-realised works with '18 classes under coordinate permutation and translation'), and at the level of games translating coordinate j is just relabelling Max vertex j's two actions — and (b) a point the paper has already conceded twice, concretely. rem:blowup-measured says the 100-vertex one-player game performs 'exactly the operation that rem:blowup-realise identifies as the obstacle', and prop:xor exhibits the mechanism (a pinned self-return giving a three-level signal, plus a threshold into which the layer enters with the opposite sign). So the anti-value obstacle was already known not to bind, with a witness; lvl:swap adds a reformulation, not a resolution.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.5237-5250 (rem:blowup-measured), l.5460-5495 (prop:xor and the paragraph after it), l.6518-6522 (prop:m3-realised).

findings.defect: Both are restatements of sentences already in frontier.tex, with arithmetic added. The alternation clause restates thm:alternation-bits' own closing line ('nothing here bounds the denominator of the rows, which is the quantity rem:blowup-realise asks about'), decorated with d >= k/|C| = Theta(1). lvl:accounting restates rem:blowup-realise's own accounting, widened from O(1) bits per level to poly(k) bits in total — a genuine but obvious relaxation, worth one clause, not a numbered result.

Partly rests on random sampling (3000 random slope matrices at m=3 for j=2, 1200 each for j=0,1, plus a stalled hill-climb), which this project does not accept as evidence — the route says so, to its credit. The non-random content is three LP infeasibilities on published one-player systems and two on the published B^2 games, all inside an ansatz whose necessity is unestablished (finding 2). The inference actually drawn — 'the step cannot be started from a one-player realisation of the previous level', and next_steps (4)'s proposed necessary condition 'each level forces a Min vertex INSIDE the inner block' — does not follow: at the only level where it is testable, the paper's 100-vertex ONE-PLAYER game realises a blow-up level with a translated layer and has no Min vertex anywhere. A proof that no one-player driven system is liftable would therefore rule out the template, not the realisation.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.5237-5250 and prop:xor; the route's own caveat 'the LP forces the off-layer constants to be strategy-independent ... infeasibility of the LP is a restriction of the true condition, not a refutation of it'. Its control experiment (lift_hits.json) is run only on uniform orientations and the route discounts it itself.

findings.defect: UNDER-claimed: this is the route's one strict strengthening of a paper theorem, and the route does not state the corollary. Since u has maximal height, h_u = h, so the closed form gives max_v H = 2h+2 exactly (attained on layers (1,1) and (1,0)/(0,1)), upgrading thm:blowup's 'at least 2h+2' and rem:blowup-measured's 'exactly 2h+2 on every seed measured' to a theorem; with a non-maximal seed u the height is exactly h + h(u) + 2, so no choice of seed makes B beat doubling. The Lean file proves only that ONE walk has length exactly 2h(u)+2, not that the maximum is.
findings.evidence: I verified the closed form exactly at k=1..5 (dimensions 3,5,7,9,11), 0 mismatches on all 2^dim vertices, in audit-level/cube.py — the route checked k<=3 only; heights 4,10,22,46,94 = 3*2^k-2 reproduced, h_u even from level 2 on confirmed.

findings.defect: Padded. Of the thirteen entries, lvl:drive-nonneg is a one-line corollary of lvl:layer-order, lvl:no-obstruction is a corollary of lvl:tower-cover + lvl:chi-cap + lvl:order-cap, lvl:finite-order is a corollary of lvl:order-cap (and defective), and lvl:rescale — correct and trivial — is used by no other result in the route. The genuinely new, load-bearing content is four items: lvl:parity-recursion, lvl:layer-order, lvl:chi-cap+lvl:order-cap (as one remark), and the lvl:layer00-exact/lvl:b2-anatomy reading of one game.

findings.defect: No defect — recording what reproduced. Every numeric claim I re-derived independently from the published data matched exactly: outmap of B2_small_nf.json equals the published B^2 with 0 ties; pi_A = 2048/3313 and pi_B = 2036/3313 at all eight layer-(0,0) strategies; no inner row reads c_4; off-layer drive max = 270545851903/778234705920; frozen inner outmap = B^1 at t=0 and = B^1(. xor e_2) at t=pi_B; fences 0.5802359785... and 0.6222488554...; covers of B^2 and B^3 by 3 and 9 Holt-Klee AUSOs; uniform orientations Holt-Klee to m=4; lvl:layer-order on the tower to dimension 11 and on TWO independent games (the 138-vertex one and prop:xor's, 0 violations each). verdict:
IS IT NEW? Mostly yes as text, but the load-bearing content is much smaller than the results list suggests, and two items shadow the paper. lvl:swap is the readout form of a triviality frontier.tex already uses (realisability is a cube-automorphism class property, prop:m3-realised) and of a concession it already makes with a witness (rem:blowup-measured + prop:xor); lvl:no-obstruction's last clause and lvl:accounting restate sentences already in thm:alternation-bits and rem:blowup-realise. lvl:hk-product is standard USO folklore, correctly flagged by the route as presumably known — but it is NOT lem:hstar-super's product (twisted, heights add, Holt-Klee fails at (4,4),(5,4),(5,5)) and must be distinguished or it reads as contradicting rem:four-ceilings. Genuinely new: lvl:parity-recursion (the strongest item, and under-claimed — it proves the blow-up height is EXACTLY 2h+2, which thm:blowup only bounds below and rem:blowup-measured only measures), lvl:layer-order, lvl:chi-cap/lvl:order-cap, and the anatomy of one game.

CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No target-equivalent oracle, no claimed algorithm, no claimed polynomial class, no claimed barrier (the route correctly claims none — it covers none of M1-M6, def:bsi, R_BR or all-switches), no claimed family and no new game built. But two structural weaknesses: (i) the "closing" of candidate obstructions (ii) and (iii) is near-vacuous work — a lower bound of the form log2 chi_HK <= m or log2 r <= m is automatically O(k) when m = 2k+1, so it could never have refuted an O(k) regime, and the three-page product apparatus buys only 2k+1 -> 1.59k; (ii) the whole positive programme rests on ONE step, the single 138-vertex game — exactly the "does a cost datum rest on one step" trap — and the paper's OTHER realised translated layer (prop:xor's 100-vertex one-player game) violates the template's hypotheses, which the route never mentions.

VERIFICATION HONESTY? Good on the exact side: I re-derived every number independently and all matched, and my Holt-Klee test reproduces the paper's known facts. The negative measurements are honestly labelled "measured", with the right caveat, and the random-sampling component is disclaimed by the route itself.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, stated more precisely than the route states it: unchanged from rem:blowup-realise — exhibit one nondegenerate stopping SSG whose improvement outmap is B^3 (dimension 7, height 22) and read off its controlled-vertex count and row denominator, or lower-bound that denominator; the route's substitute gap (driven liftability) is both unsatisfied by the only known level-two realisation (its frozen inner system stops realising B^1 at drive ~0.1865 while the off-layer drive reaches 0.34764) and unnecessary (prop:xor's one-player game realises a translated layer with a non-constant drive and inner rows reading both outer coordinates), so it is a strictly stronger and possibly unsatisfiable statement standing in for the real one.

BETTER OR WORSE? The whole package would make the paper WORSE: about five pages of machinery for a constant-factor improvement on a bound that is trivially capped, one result (lvl:finite-order) that closes an open question of thm:readout-realise without proving it, a design template contradicted by the paper's own second example, a product lemma that reads as contradicting rem:four-ceilings, and a misattribution of the route's framing to rem:blowup-realise. A trimmed subset would make it BETTER, roughly one page:
INTEGRATE — (1) lvl:parity-recursion, as a proposition right after thm:blowup, WITH the corollary the route omits: height exactly h + h(u) + 2, hence exactly 2h+2 at a maximal seed, which turns rem:blowup-measured's measurement into a theorem and says no seed beats doubling (I verified the formula at k=1..5). (2) lvl:layer-order and its corollary lvl:drive-nonneg, three lines from thm:blowup plus lem:switch, verified on the tower to dimension 11 and on two independent games — a constraint on EVERY realisation, not on a template. (3) lvl:chi-cap and lvl:order-cap as ONE two-sentence remark appended to thm:min-count: both necessary conditions the paper has are capped by the dimension, so neither can ever force more than m Min vertices; add the one-line proof that uniform orientations are LP orientations hence Holt-Klee, citing Holt-Klee/Gaertner-Morris-Ruest as the paper already does. (4) one clause in rem:blowup-realise recording lvl:accounting (poly(k) total, not O(1) per level, suffices for the pivot's conclusion). (5) lvl:pin/lvl:layer00-exact/lvl:b2-anatomy as a short ANATOMY remark on prop:b2-realised — "this particular design pins its outer pair, so its translated layer is one frozen system at drive 2036/3313 inside the window (0.58024, 0.62225)" — explicitly paired with prop:xor's game as the counterpoint that the shape is not forced, and with the observation that off layer (0,0) the drive leaves the window.
DO NOT INTEGRATE — lvl:finite-order (unproved as stated; at most keep "the minimum order of a realising readout system is at most 2^m, so the order half of the monotone route's question (D) is settled and the dyadic-leaky half is not"); lvl:hk-product and lvl:tower-cover as propositions (a footnote at most, and only with the twisted/untwisted distinction spelled out); lvl:rescale (trivial and unused); lvl:liftability-negative as a constraint on realisations (if kept at all, only as "a template we tried, with its measured failures", never as evidence about what a realisation must contain); lvl:swap as a lemma "removing the obstacle"; lvl:parity-nonlocal beyond one sentence. And next_steps (4)'s proposed necessary condition should be dropped or reformulated: as stated it is undercut by the paper's own one-player realisation of B(2-cube).
